layers.description: two curved dragon horns — Tuk's dragon/monster signal (the dragon is Tuk wearing horns)

a domed silver helm with side flaps — the knight signal for the head, pairing with the sword. One helmet for the whole troupe, cut 16px wide: that is where ada's and rosa's hair actually ends. Their heads measure 18, but the outermost column each side is outline, and the outline colour is the background colour — so reaching it would buy nothing visible. Sized to the hair, not to any one wearer, which is why it swamps milo, and is meant to: it is a shared prop out of one trunk, and it does not fit everyone. Open-faced by design: the dome closes in a dark brow edge on the last row above the face box, and the flaps drop only through the columns free of expression ink, so every expression still reads underneath. No visor, nose guard or chin strap — anything crossing the face would cover the brows and mouth the expressions are drawn with. Hair below the rim is left showing on purpose; that is what a helmet does
a gold crown — kings and queens; authored once, fits every human head

a long fringe hanging over the eyes — hair the wearer can't see past; strip it with an explicit null when it is cut or spelled away. Ada-only: unlike a crown or a hat, a fringe IS hair, so it is authored in one hair colour and can only ever match one head. It is drawn in Ada's deep purple, and read as a wig on the other three

a wide-brimmed pointed hat, tip crooked to one side — the brim is the witch signal, no other layer has one. Rosa-only: she is the short actor, so her face box sits lowest in the cell and leaves the most room above it for the cone

a slim silver band under a single jewelled peak — the princess signal, and deliberately silver where the crown is gold, so the two never depend on silhouette alone. Rosa and Ada only: it is the layer a story reaches for when a girl is royal, and scoping it keeps the director from dressing a king in it

a wide pair of butterfly wings behind the shoulders — the butterfly's reveal, a ladybug's flight, a fairy's costume. Drawn in morpho blue so they read against every wearer's own colours, and deliberately wider than the body: the wing tips run off the screen edges by design, which is what the art's bleed_x declares. Not for tuk or bruno — a side-on quadruped and a body that already fills the frame both need a differently oriented pair, which does not exist yet

an American football — a small painted oval with white end stripes and laces, held in one hand. Human-only like every front_prop, and not by taste: the slot registers on the wearer's hand anchor, and only the four humans have one. Deliberately small at 8x5 base pixels; the hand has far more room than that, so the size is a legibility choice rather than a limit. No `o` anywhere in it, which is why it reads: 23 of the 40 pixels behind this prop are bruno's own salmon skin, and he is the one who carries it, so a salmon-topped ball melts into the arm holding it. The body is r -> d, which sits behind nobody, and the white stripes and laces do the work

a crooked wooden wand with a glowing tip — long, narrow, a cut branch rather than a turned dowel, lit at the end as though a spell is about to leave it. Two base pixels across at its widest, with the centre-line drifting three pixels out over its length so the tip leans away from the wearer: the face sits to the LEFT of the hand on every human, so leaning right carries the tip off the face instead of into it. The wood is o -> r -> d and the dark end carries it, because the palette has no brown and the two obvious warm tones are the ones that vanish — `o` sits behind the wand on rosa, bruno and ada, `y` on rosa, milo and bruno — so `o` is only a one-pixel lit edge. The grip is told by colour rather than girth, since a handle wider than the shaft reads as a club at this size. The tip is cyan with a white-hot core, unoutlined so it reads as emissive, and cyan because it is the only colour with real contrast against all three things the tip crosses: the dark screen, rosa's gold hair and ada's purple. It shares that cyan with the wings, which is intended — the magic props read as one family. Human-only like every front_prop, and not by taste: the slot registers on the wearer's hand anchor, and only the four humans have one. 13 base pixels tall, the measured ceiling — at 14 ada starts covering her own brows and at 15 milo does too

a plume of dragon fire, pouring from below the muzzle and falling down the chest — for the beat a dragon actually breathes, not for the whole role. White-hot core with a gold edge and deliberately no `o` or `r` in it: tuk's own chest is 96 pixels of `o` and 44 of `r`, so a conventionally orange flame would vanish into the dragon breathing it, and the hottest part of a real flame is white anyway. Tuk-only, and it is the reason he has a front_prop anchor at all: the slot registers on the wearer's `hand`, which for a quadruped is the muzzle rather than a hand — he cannot hold anything, and `fits` keeps the human props off him. Hangs downward from that anchor via dy, and starts one row below the mouth so every expression still reads above it — including surprised, whose open jaw dips lowest

a silver blade with a gold crossguard, held up in front — the knight-and-hero signal, first item of the held-prop slot. An object like the crown, so it fits every human; it overlaps the wearer's body by design (there is no room beside a 6x actor), so its read comes from its own outline, not what's behind it

a pair of clubbed antennae rising from the head — the insect signal, and the half of a butterfly reveal that wings alone cannot carry: wings without antennae read as a person wearing wings. Pale stalks on purpose, because anything clearing the head is drawn against the screen, and the screen is the same colour as an outline

tall bunny ears with a salmon inner, above the same whiskers `whiskers` draws — the rabbit signal as ONE layer, because headwear is a single slot and ears and whiskers cannot each hold it. The bottom twelve rows of this grid are `whiskers` verbatim and both sidecars carry the same dx 0 / dy 18, so a story can swap the cat for the rabbit and the whiskers do not move. The ears stop at Pip's outline row, the last one above his face box: every brow the angry, sad, scared and surprised overlays draw begins on the row below it, and headwear draws OVER the expression. White with a salmon inner so they read against the screen above the head and against gold fur below it. They cover Pip's own pointed ears on purpose — that is what makes him a rabbit rather than a cat wearing something

three whiskers a side sweeping out past the body from beside the mouth — the cat signal, and Pip's own pointed ears do the other half, which is why this layer is whiskers alone. Routed through the one corridor all twelve expressions leave empty: the eyes bottom out at base row 10.5 and the widest row of the mouth spans base cols 12.5 to 17, so the whiskers run below the eyes, stop short of the mouth, and cover no expression pixel on either wearer — with nothing to spare on tuk, whose mouth is wider and whose face box sits further left. White, because the outer half of every whisker is drawn against the screen and the screen is the outline colour

sfx_catalog.sound: a rushing air sweep, low to high
sfx_catalog.use: fast movement — flying, swooping, someone carried off, a dash on or off stage
sfx_catalog.avoid: magic (that's sparkle) and mood-setting wind; it reads as one motion, not weather

sfx_catalog.use: a big creature's voice or big anger — dragons, giants, Bruno-scale fury
sfx_catalog.avoid: more than once per scene; it loses its power on repeat

sfx_catalog.use: a sword drawn, armor donned, a shiny treasure revealed — heroic punctuation
sfx_catalog.avoid: non-metal reveals; it strongly implies metal

sfx_catalog.use: fire breath, a blaze flaring up, dramatic danger arriving
sfx_catalog.avoid: cozy background fires; it reads as an event, not ambience

sfx_catalog.use: wonder, resolution, happy endings — and the player's title sound, so every story ships it
sfx_catalog.avoid: tension or danger; it always means all-is-well

sfx_catalog.use: riding, a hurried journey, hooves arriving
a horse's voice — usually Tuk in a horse role
sfx_catalog.avoid: any creature that isn't a horse

sfx_catalog.sound: a glittery rising cascade of pings
sfx_catalog.use: magic, transformation, fairy dust, Miss Moon's hosting flourish
a dog's voice, or a small critter raising the alarm — usually Pip
sfx_catalog.avoid: creatures that wouldn't bark; squeak covers the rest of the small-critter range

sfx_catalog.use: a small critter's voice or excitement — Pip's signature
sfx_catalog.avoid: big creatures; a big thing squeaking is a joke, so only do it on purpose

voices.description: Miss Moon's dedicated host voice — warm, bubbly, a light Southern drawl, identical in every story
Bruno — low, gruff, weathered; a British stage voice
Milo — mid, noble, earnest; a British stage voice
Ada — mid, warm, steady; a British stage voice
Rosa — bright, young; an American child
